SinLines Privacy Policy

SinLines is a reading app: you read books, swipe through lines in sinLes, save the ones you love and keep a reading streak. This policy explains, in plain words, what SinLines keeps about you, why, where, for how long and who else sees it. SinLines is run by Ananth Babu G ("we").

In short

  • You need an account to read and to add books. Without one you can still look through the books and try a few sinLes lines, and we keep no account data about you.
  • With an account, we keep only what SinLines needs to work: your username, your place in your books, your reading days, the lines you save, the words you look up and any feedback you send.
  • We don't ask for your email address, your phone number, your contacts or your location.
  • We never sell your data, and SinLines shows no ads from other companies.
  • Books you add from your phone and your settings stay on your phone, and only the account that added a book can see it.
  • You can download your data, turn off optional things and delete your account at any time.

What SinLines keeps, and why

If you have an account, on our server:

  • Your account: your username, the date you joined, your birth year (so we know whether teen mode applies) and, for readers under 18, a parent's email address. Your password is handled by our login provider and stored only in a scrambled (hashed) form; we never see it. Behind the scenes your login address is made from your username (username@users.sinlines.com); it is not a real email address and nothing is ever sent to it.
  • Your choices: which version of these terms you accepted and when, and whether marketing and analytics are on or off.
  • Your place in your books: for each book, how far you have read, so you can carry on from another phone.
  • Your reading days: for each day, the minutes and lines you read, whether you met your daily goal and which books you finished. This is what keeps your streak.
  • Your saved lines: the sinLes lines you save.
  • My words: the words you look up while reading, with the book you met each one in and when.
  • Your devices: for each phone or browser your account is signed in on, a name (like "iPhone 13 · iOS"), a random id the app made for it, and when it was last used. An account can be on at most 3 devices; one not used for 90 days stops counting.
  • SinLines Premium: whether you have it, until when, and where it came from (a test for now; later the App Store or Google Play). When you open a premium book, we note which book and when, so that one account can't download more than 20 different books a day.
  • sinLes counts (analytics): when a card is viewed, a line is saved or a book is opened from a card, we record which line, what happened, when, and your user id. We use this to see which lines readers like, and you can turn it off. Guests' counts carry no user id.
  • Feedback: messages you send us from Help, linked to your account.

For everyone, briefly: when the app talks to our server, the server sees technical details such as your IP address and the time of the request. These sit in short-term logs kept by our hosting provider to run and protect the service. We don't use them to track you.

If you email us: we get your email address and your message, and use them only to answer you.

Only on your phone (never sent to us): books and PDFs you add from your phone and your place in them (only the account that added a book can see it), your reader and reminder settings, the list of sinLes cards you've seen, the book you read last (used for your reminders) and copies of catalog books you've opened. Reminders are made on your phone; we don't collect any notification token.

What the assistant sees: the assistant works on your phone. It reads our public book list to suggest books. What you type to it is not kept and is not sent to us or to any AI company.

Where your data is kept

  • On your phone: the things listed above, until you remove them or delete the app.
  • On our server: we use Supabase for our database, logins and book files. Your account data is stored in Supabase's Tokyo region, in Japan.
  • Backups: once a week an automated job on GitHub copies our database, encrypts the copy (AES-256) and keeps it for 90 days. GitHub keeps data in the United States. Only the encrypted copy is stored, and it can't be read without our passphrase.

How long we keep it

  • Account data (everything in the server list above): for as long as you have an account. When you ask to delete your account, we wait 7 days in case you change your mind, then delete it for good. It disappears from our backups when they expire, within 90 days.
  • sinLes counts: kept to improve the feed. When your account is deleted, they are no longer linked to you.
  • Premium book downloads: 30 days.
  • Feedback: kept to improve SinLines. When your account is deleted, it is kept without your account attached.
  • Server logs: a short time, as set by our hosting provider.
  • Emails to us: as long as we need them to help you.
  • On your phone: until you clear it, sign out (which clears your reading days from the phone) or delete the app.

Who we share it with

We never sell your data or share it for advertising. Only these companies handle it, and only to run SinLines for us:

  • Supabase: hosts our database, logins and book files.
  • GitHub: runs our weekly backup job and stores the encrypted copies.
  • Our email provider: holds our support mailbox, if you email us.
  • Apple App Store and Google Play: deliver the app and, when SinLines Premium is on sale, take payments. They handle your payment details; we never see them.

We may share data if the law requires it, for example to answer a valid court order, and only as much as required.

Your rights

Wherever you live, you can:

  • See and download your data: Settings > Legal > Download my data gives you a copy in a standard format (JSON).
  • Correct it: most of it is yours to change in the app; for anything else, write to us.
  • Delete it: Profile > Delete account, or on our website. Logging in again within 7 days cancels the deletion.
  • Change your mind: turn marketing or analytics off at any time in Settings > Legal.
  • Ask questions or complain: write to us at sinlines.read@gmail.com. You can also complain to the data protection authority where you live (see below).

We answer requests as quickly as we can, and within the time the law where you live allows.

Children and teens

  • When you make an account we ask for your birth year.
  • Under 18: SinLines switches to teen mode: no marketing, no referral rewards and no analytics. We ask for a parent's email address and their agreement. We are building a fuller way for parents to confirm their consent.
  • Under 13: a parent's consent is needed before making an account.
  • Parents can ask us to see or delete their child's data at any time by writing to sinlines.read@gmail.com.

Contact and grievances

For any question, request or complaint about your data, write to our grievance contact: sinlines.read@gmail.com. We'll reply as soon as we can.

SinLines is run by Ananth Babu G, Koppal, Karnataka, India.

Rules where you live

India: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and Rules 2025

What the law says, simply: an app must tell you clearly what it collects and why, use your data only for that purpose with your consent (or for a few lawful uses), keep it safe, delete it when it is no longer needed and tell you and the Data Protection Board of India about any data breach. You have the right to information about your data, to correct and erase it, to have your complaints handled and to name someone to act for you if you can't. Children are people under 18: their data needs a parent's verifiable consent, and they must not be tracked or targeted with ads. The Rules 2025 set out how this works in practice; most of their duties apply from May 2027.

How SinLines follows it:

  • This policy is our notice, in plain language, with each thing we keep and why.
  • We ask you to accept it before you use SinLines, and you can withdraw optional consents (marketing, analytics) at any time in Settings > Legal.
  • We keep only what SinLines needs and delete accounts 7 days after you ask.
  • Your account data is stored in Japan (Supabase's Tokyo region) and our encrypted backups in the United States. The Act allows this; if the Government of India ever restricts a country, we will follow that.
  • Your data is protected as described in "How your data is protected".
  • You can see, download, correct and delete your data in the app, or write to sinlines.read@gmail.com. You can also name a person to act for you by writing to us.
  • Readers under 18 get teen mode: no tracking for analytics, no marketing and no targeted ads (SinLines has no ads at all). We ask for a parent's consent and are building a fuller way to verify it before the Rules require it.
  • If a breach puts your data at risk, we will tell you and the Data Protection Board as the law requires.
  • If you are unhappy with our answer, you can complain to the Data Protection Board of India.
Europe and the UK: GDPR

What the law says, simply: an app needs a lawful reason to use your data, must collect only what it needs and must keep it safe. You have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict and take away (port) your data, to object to some uses and to withdraw consent at any time. Children below their country's age of digital consent (between 13 and 16; 13 in the UK) need a parent's consent where an app relies on consent.

How SinLines follows it:

  • Our reasons: running your account, sync and streaks is needed to provide SinLines to you (contract). sinLes counts and security logs rely on our legitimate interest in improving and protecting SinLines, and you can turn analytics off. Marketing is only with your consent.
  • Your rights: download your data (Settings > Legal), correct it, delete your account, turn optional uses off, or write to sinlines.read@gmail.com for anything else, including restriction and objection.
  • Transfers: your data is stored in Supabase's Tokyo region, in Japan, and our encrypted backups with GitHub in the United States. Where data leaves the EU or UK, our providers use the safeguards the law requires, such as Standard Contractual Clauses.
  • Children: under-18s get teen mode, and accounts for children under the age your country sets need a parent's consent.
  • Complaints: you can complain to the data protection authority in your country, or the ICO in the UK.
United States: California (CCPA/CPRA) and children (COPPA)

What the law says, simply: in California you have the right to know what personal information an app collects, to delete and correct it, to opt out of it being sold or shared for advertising, and not to be treated differently for using these rights. Other states have similar laws. COPPA protects children under 13: an app must get a parent's consent before collecting their personal information.

How SinLines follows it:

  • We collect only what is listed in this policy, for the reasons given.
  • We do not sell or share your personal information, and we use none of it for advertising, so there is nothing to opt out of.
  • You can see, download, correct and delete your data in the app or by writing to sinlines.read@gmail.com, and using these rights never changes how SinLines works for you.
  • SinLines is not aimed at children under 13; an account for a child under 13 needs a parent's consent. A parent who believes their child under 13 made an account can write to us and we will delete it.
Other countries

What the law says, simply: many countries have privacy laws that work much like the ones above: tell people what you collect, use it fairly, keep it safe and let them see and delete it.

How SinLines follows it: we give everyone, wherever they live, the same protections and rights described in this policy. If your local law gives you more, write to sinlines.read@gmail.com and we will honour it.

Data and cache

On your phone: books and PDFs you add (seen only by the account that added them), your place in them, a copy of My words for each account, your settings, your reminders, the sinLes cards you've seen, your reading days (a copy), copies of catalog books you've opened (the cache, so books open faster and work offline) and the random id of this device. Your login is kept in the phone's secure storage (the Keychain on iPhone, the Keystore on Android). In a web browser it is kept in the browser's own storage.

On our server: your account, your place in catalog books, your reading days, your saved lines, My words, sinLes counts and feedback (see "What SinLines keeps").

To clear things on your phone:

  • Remove a book you added: Browse > My uploads, then press and hold the book.
  • Remove a looked-up word: Menu > My words, then tap × next to it.
  • Sign out: Menu > Log out. This removes your login and your reading days from the phone; they stay safe in your account.
  • Clear the cache (the copies of catalog books): on Android, Settings > Apps > SinLines > Storage > Clear cache. iPhone has no clear-cache button for single apps; it clears the cache by itself when it runs low on space.
  • Remove everything SinLines keeps on the phone: delete the app. On Android you can also use Settings > Apps > SinLines > Storage > Clear storage.

Clearing your phone doesn't delete your account. To delete what is on our server, use Profile > Delete account.

Marketing and referrals
  • Marketing is off unless you turn it on (Settings > Legal > Marketing). If you turn it on, we may tell you about new books and features inside the app or with a notification. Turn it off at any time.
  • Referrals: you can share SinLines with friends by sending a link from your phone's share menu. You choose who gets it. We never upload, read or keep your contacts or address book.
  • We never sell your data and SinLines shows no ads from other companies.
  • Teens (under 18): no marketing and no referral rewards.
How your data is protected
  • On the way: everything the app sends to or receives from our server travels over HTTPS (TLS), so others on the network can't read it.
  • On our server: our provider, Supabase, encrypts the stored data (encryption at rest).
  • Passwords: handled by Supabase's login service and stored only in a hashed form. We can't see your password.
  • Only you see your data: our database checks every request (row-level security), so a signed-in reader can only read and change their own account's data, and guests can't read any of it.
  • Premium books: only our server hands them out, after checking your premium, your device and the daily limit, as a link that works for 60 seconds.
  • On your phone: your login is kept in the phone's secure storage (the Keychain on iPhone, the Keystore on Android).
  • Backups: encrypted (AES-256) before they are stored, and kept for 90 days.
  • Keys: the master key to our database is never put in the app. It is kept only by us.

No system is perfectly secure. If something goes wrong and your data is at risk, we will tell you and the authorities as the law requires.

Changes to this policy

When we change this policy we'll update the version and date at the top, and the app will ask you to agree again before you carry on.
